articleTitle: The benefits of coding over routing in a randomized setting
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A novel randomized network coding approach for robust, distributed transmission and compression of information in networks is presented, and its advantages over routing-based approaches is demonstrated.

articleTitle: On the capacity of a biometrical identification system
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We investigate fundamental properties of biometrical identification systems. We focus on the capacity, i.e. a measure for the number of individuals that can be reliably identified. It can be expressed using standard information-theoretical concepts.

articleTitle: A game-theoretic approach to power allocation in frequency-selective gaussian interference channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Throughput and delay optimal resource allocation in multiaccess fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Network coding from a network flow perspective
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Precise connections between algebraic network coding and network flows are explained in this article. Our combinatorial formulations offer new insights, mathematical simplicity, and lead to a substantially tighter upper bound on the coding field size required for a given connection problem than that in R. Koetter et al.

articleTitle: Low complexity algebraic multicast network codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Analysis of transmit antenna selection/maximal-ratio combining in Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: An analytical bit error rate (BER) expression for a transmit antenna selection scheme with maximal-ratio combining at the receiver (TAS/MRC) is derived. The expression shows that this system asymptotically achieves a full diversity order.

articleTitle: Stopping sets in codes from designs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The size of the smallest stopping set in LDPC codes helps in analyzing their performance under iterative decoding, just a minimum distance helps in analyzing the performance under maximum likelihood decoding. We study stopping sets in LDPC codes arising from 2-designs, in particular LDPC codes derived from projective and Euclidean geometries. We derive upper and lower bounds on the size of the smallest stopping set in such codes, and provide examples of codes that achieve these bounds.

articleTitle: Optimal Incremental-redundancy strategy for type-II hybrid ARQ
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Given a type-II hybrid ARQ scheme, we propose a general solution to find the optimal partitioning of n-k parity bits over at most M transmissions. The solution is in terms of maximizing the average code rate for a given puncturing pattern.

articleTitle: Minimum energy communication over a relay channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A new achievable rate for cooperative diversity based on generalized writing on dirty paper
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Joint decoding and phase estimation: an exercise in factor graphs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On two-user fading gaussian broadcast channels with perfect channel state information at the receivers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the log determinant of noncentral Wishart matrices
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we show that the expected log determinant of a complex noncentral Wishart matrix is an increasing function of the noncentrality parameter. This demonstrates that the mutual information corresponding to an isotropically distributed Gaussian input to a multiantenna Ricean fading channel is nondecreasing in the line-of-sight component.

articleTitle: Combined shaping and precoding for interference cancellation at low SNR
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We consider multi dimensional dirty paper coding at low SNR, and propose a low rate precoding scheme which combines MMSE estimation, dithering and a variant of nested codes, based on concatenation of a "syndrome dilution" code and a "syndrome-to-coset" modulation code.

articleTitle: Multiplicity assignments for algebraic soft-decoding of reed-solomon codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Efficient interpolation and factorization in algebraic soft-decision decoding of reed-solonion codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Ad hoc wireless networks with noisy links
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the complexity of ml lattice decoders for decoding linear full rate space-time codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Simulation-based computation of information rates: upper and lower bounds
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: It has recently become feasible to compute information rates of finite-state source/channel models with memory. Such methods can also be used to compute upper and lower bounds on the information rate of very general (nonfinite-state) channels with memory by means of finite-state approximations. Further numerical bounds are obtained from reduced-state computations.

articleTitle: Very efficient wireless fyequency usage based on pseudo-coherent addition of multipath signals using kronecker product with rows of dft matrix
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Universal discrete denoising: known channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A universal discrete denoiser is a scheme that (asymptotically) attains the optimum distribution-dependent performance with no a priori knowledge of the source statistics. Despite the importance of the problem, there is no universal discrete denoiser available in the literature. The main contribution of this work is a discrete universal denoiser (DUDE) that attains optimum (distribution-dependent) performance with computational complexity that grows linearly with the data size.

articleTitle: Optimum ARQ design: a dynamic programming approach
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A hybrid ARQ scheme as an incremental accumulation of redundancy at the receiver is viewed in this article. A hybrid ARQ design problem is formulated as a search for the sequence of redundancies maximizing throughput or minimizing delay. The optimization is performed within the framework of a Markov decision process. The state space is defined as the total accumulated redundancy at the receiver. The transition probabilities model the error-correcting capability of the code and properties of the channel. Employing a dynamic programming approach, the optimum sequence of redundancies is characterized.

articleTitle: A combinatoric superposition method for constructing low density parity check codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper presents a combinatoric method for constructing low density parity check (LDPC) codes. Two classes of LDPC codes are constructed and they perform well with iterative decoding. Codes in one class are quasicyclic which can be encoded in linear-time with simple shift-registers.

articleTitle: Low complexity list detection for high-rate multiple-antenna channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A class of ternary sequence sets having a zero-correlation zone for even and odd correlation functions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A class of ternary sequence sets having a zero-correlation zone (zcz) is presented, based on Hadamard matrix, is presented.

articleTitle: Jensen-renyi divergence measure: theoretical and computational perspectives
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Degrees of freedom in underspread mimo fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Lossless data compression with error correcting codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Existing zero-error variable-length data compression algorithms suffer from sensitivity to transmission errors and error propagation across packets when used in packet-based data transmission through noisy channels. We propose a new approach to lossless data compression based on error correcting codes and the block-sorting transform. The proposed data compression scheme is compared with the universal algorithm for a four-state Markov chain in comparison with LZ (gzip) and a conventional BWT-based compressor (bzip). Although the comparison is quite encouraging, the main motivation and advantages of our scheme over the conventional separation-based approach accrue in the joint source/channel setting.

articleTitle: On the achievable region for multiple description source codes on Gaussian sources
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We demonstrate inconsistencies in prior results on the achievable region for multiple description (MD) source codes on i.i.d. Gaussian sources with the squared error distortion measure. We then describe the complete region.

articleTitle: Coupled receiver-decoders for low rate turbo codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the capacity of correlated mimo channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The on-off fading channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Lowering the error-rate floors of moderate-length high-rate irregular ldpc codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Coding for the mimo broadcast channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On compression for robust estimation in sensor networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes the sensor network, which is an unreliable, with measurement available at central decoder. The paper also compares the distributed compression with the distributed coding of raw vector measurements.

articleTitle: A generalized Blahut-Arimoto algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Kavcic proposed in (A. Kavcic, 2001) an algorithm that apparently finds the mutual-information-rate-maximizing parameters of a Markov source at the input to an indecomposable finite-state channel. In this paper we prove that the stationary points of this algorithm indeed correspond one-to-one to the critical points of the information-rate curve. Kavcic's algorithm can be considered as a generalized Blahut-Arimoto algorithm, as it includes as special cases the classical Blahut-Arimoto algorithm for discrete memoryless channels (DMCs) and the solution to finding the capacity-achieving input distribution for finite-state channels with no noise (C.E. Shannon, 1948).

articleTitle: Sum power iterative waterfilling for Gaussian vector broadcast channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: An efficient algorithm for computing the sum capacity of vector broadcast channel is obtained in this paper. This algorithm utilizes the duality between broadcast and multiple access channels and the Kuhn-Tucker conditions of sum power multiple access channel.

articleTitle: A property of the intrinsic mutual information
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Optimal puncturing distributions for rate-compatible low-density parity-check codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Routing and data compression in sensor networks: stochastic models for sensor data that guarantee scalability
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the compression of correlated data samples in multihop sensor network by means of distributed source coding techniques under plausible stochastic models. This paper shows that there are cases where high density sensor networks are not only possible but increased density can potentially be used to increase the precision of the measurements or decrease the transmission error. The routing algorithms and reencoding of the sensor data is proposed in this paper to provide a perfect feasible sensor networks.

articleTitle: X-codes: error control with unknowable inputs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper studies a class of codes used for digital system test compaction technique. An X-code produces a hash from an input vector in a way that guarantees that errors in the inputs change the resulting hash despite the presence of unknowable inputs. The value of an unknowable input cannot be inferred. Some classes of X-codes overlap with deterministic combinatorial group testing (CGT) solutions provides constructive bounds.

articleTitle: On minimizing total weighted square correlation of cdma systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Antenna selection for MIMO-OFDM spatial multiplexing system
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Transmit antenna selection is a promising closed-loop approach to introduce transmit-diversity for MIMO system. It offers performance improvement compared to the open loop schemes with equivalent complexity by only using low rate feedback link. Two categories of selection criteria were reported, which are capacity-oriented criteria (R. Blum, et al., 2002)and performance-oriented criteria (R.W. Heath, et al., 2001). In this paper, we focus on the later case. We present an analytical bound of transmit-diversity gain provided by antenna selection in flat fading channels. An antenna selection criterion is proposed for MIMO-OFDM in frequency selective fading channels.

articleTitle: Designing LDPC codes using cyclic shifts
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper presents a method to construct LDPC codes by arranging cyclic shift matrices. These codes perform well at various rates for moderate code length. By substituting those cyclic shifts for their Kronecker products with small random permutations, the performance of long codes can be improved, while the structure facilitates hardware implementation.

articleTitle: Bit error rate estimation for turbo decoding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We propose a method for on-line estimation of the bit error rate (BER) during turbo decoding. The Gaussian assumption has been widely used in analysing the convergence behavior of turbo codes.

articleTitle: Further analytic properties of exit-like curves and applications
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Network error correction
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the error correction in all existing communication networks which is done on a link-by-link approach. We define a network coding and a distributed error correction in a network is considered when a source message is transmitted to a set of receiving nodes on a network. Network generalizations of the Hamming bound and Gilbert-Varshamov bound are obtained.

articleTitle: On braided block codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Two families of braided block codes are analyzed, tightly braided block codes and sparsely braided block codes. Bounds on the free distance of tightly braided block codes are derived. Asymptotic iterative decoding performance of sparsely braided block codes is studied.

articleTitle: Quasicyclic low density parity check codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this work, the construction of low density parity check codes (LDPCs) from circulant permutation matrices is investigated. It is shown that such codes can not have a Tanner graph representation with girth larger than 12, and a relatively loose necessary and sufficient condition for the code to have a girth of 6, 8, 10 or 12 is derived. These results suggest that families of LDPC codes with such girth values are relatively easy to obtain and consequently, additional parameters such as the minimum distance or the number of redundant check sums should be considered.

articleTitle: Reachback capacity with non-interfering nodes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The exact symbol and bit error probabilities of coherent M-ary PSK
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The noncentral t-distribution that is used to evaluate the symbol-error probability of coherent M-ary phase-shift keying (PSK) is showed. We also give a method to obtain the exact bit-error probability for the binary reflected Gray mapping, and we note that the new expression reveals an error in previously published results.

articleTitle: Stable scheduling policies for fading wireless channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes the stable scheduling policies for fading wireless channels. The scheduling policies and their various modifications: at any time k, given the current channel state s[k] is studied in this paper.

articleTitle: A soft-in/soft-out list sequential(liss) decoder for turbo schemes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Throughput scaling for heterogeneous networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes the role of wired infrastructure in the context of throughput of the wireless system, particularly when the access points are comparable to the nodes themselves. This paper also discusses how the transport capacity scales as a function of the number of nodes and access points and derives both lower and upper bounds to the transport capacity.

articleTitle: On the duality between general multiple-access/broadcast channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Capacity characterization for the noncoherent block-independent awgn channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the rate-distortion region for separate encoding of correlated sources
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the two correlated sources encoded by two separate encoders. The coding strategy used in this paper is based on time-sharing of rate-distortion codes. The paper focuses on the development of an alternative coding strategy, with the aim of closing the existing gap to the Berger-Tung outer bound.

articleTitle: Optimum power allocation and complete characterization of the impact of correlation on the capacity of miso systems with different csi at the transmitter
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Asymptotic capacity of multicarrier transmission over a fading channel with feedback
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We study the asymptotic capacity of multicarrier transmission through a frequency-selective fading channel with limited feedback. The rate at which the capacity increases is characterized as a function of the number of subchannels N for the uniform power distribution over an optimized subset of channels, and optimal water filling. For Rayleigh fading, we also consider a finite-precision rate control scheme and show that the O(log N) increase in data rate can be achieved with a feedback rate, which grows as O(log/sup 3/ N). If the number of active subchannels is bounded, then the capacity grows only as O(loglog N).

articleTitle: Capacity of finite state markov channels with general inputs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On single-symbol and double-symbol decodable STBCs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A characterization of all single-symbol decodable designs (SSDD) (with or without full-diversity) is presented and a rate-one, double-symbol decodable, full-diversity coordinate-interleaved orthogonal design based on CIOD is given for eight transmit antennas.

articleTitle: Network information theory for wireless communications
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Design methods for irregular repeat accumulate codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We optimize the low-complexity random-like ensemble of irregular repeat accumulate (IRA) codes for binary-input symmetric channels in the large blocklength limit. IRA codes Jin, H et al. (2000) are special subclasses of both irregular LDPCs and irregular turbo codes. We present numerical results for the BIAWGNC and formulate the density evolution (DE) Richardson, TJ et al. (2001) for IRA codes. We study the stability condition of the fixed-point corresponding to zero BER.

articleTitle: New constructions for optical orthogonal codes, distinct difference sets and synchronous optical orthogonal codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Reduced-complexity soft-ln-soft-out decoding of variable-length codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Full cmos min-sum analog iterative decoder
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Information-theoretic and communication-theoretic optimal power allocation for fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Conditional Lempel-Ziv complexity and its application to source coding theorem with side information
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper proposes the conditional LZ complexity and analyzes its property. Especially, we show an inequality corresponding to Ziv's inequality concerning a distinct parsing of a pair of sequences. Further, as a byproduct of the result, we show a simple proof of the asymptotical optimality of Ziv's universal source coding algorithm with side information.

articleTitle: Efficient decoding of (binary) cyclic codes above the correction capacity of the code using grobner bases
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Stopping set distribution of LDPC code ensembles
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of two quantities: the distribution of stopping sets, and the stopping number s/sup */-the size of the smallest nonempty stopping set in a code and use it to bound the error probability of LDPC codes with large blocklength. We derive an expression for the normalized average stopping set distribution of regular and irregular LDPC codes and use it to obtain a critical fraction of the block length above which codes have exponentially many stopping sets of that size.

articleTitle: Design and iterative decoding of networks of many small codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Multiple window-sliding search
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the error floor analysis of turbo codes: weight spectrum estimation (WSE) scheme
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient method to find the smallest-weight codewords of a turbo code with specific interleavers. This enables us to obtain accurate approximations to the error floor performance of turbo codes.

articleTitle: Modulo-lattice reduction in precoding schemes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the use of modulo arithmetics in the precoding scheme for N-dimensional data symbols. The transmission scheme employing modulo reduction mod-/spl Lambda/ precoding is an attractive strategy when transmitting over AWGN channels, which suffer from additive noise, and an additional interference term, which is already known at the transmitter side. The capacity of channels and the use of optimum lattice quantizers for minimum error entropy approach applying numerical optimization are also studied.

articleTitle: Analysis of nonbinary ldpc codes using gaussian approximation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Geometrical uniformity of a class of space-time trellis codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The impossibility of pseudotelepathy without quantum entanglement
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In a pseudotelepathy game, communication can be entirely replaced by quantum entanglement. We provide, for the first proposed arid simplest two-player game of this type, the proof that communication is indeed necessary to win with certainty if no quantum entanglement is shared by the players. This completes the game's analysis and shows its "pseudotelepathic" properties.

articleTitle: Detailed representation of irregular LDPC code ensembles and density evolution
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We construct new families of low-density parity-check (LDPC) code ensembles which are subensembles of conventional irregular LDPC code ensembles and develop density evolution for those ensembles. Further, we find an ensemble which has a better threshold than that of its super ensemble.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling for iterative decoding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Low complexity ML detection based on the search for the closest lattice point
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The design of maximum likelihood detection algorithms for linear multidimensional constellations and lattice codes transmitted over Gaussian fading channels is considered. The linearity of the constellations over the field of complex numbers facilitates the design of maximum likelihood detectors using number theoretic tools for searching the closest lattice point. In particular, the Pohst enumeration method and the Schnorr-Euchner refinement of the Pohst strategy are used to develop two maximum likelihood detection algorithms. The first algorithm is shown to offer a significant reduction in complexity compared to the Viterbo-Boutros implementation of the Pohst strategy. The second algorithm is more suited to maximum likelihood detection than the Agrell et al. implementation of the Schnorr-Euchner strategy. Further, the two algorithms are compared to extract insights on the lowest complexity approach in different scenarios. The results obtained indicate that the distance between the nulling and cancellation solution and the maximum likelihood solution plays a major role in determining the lowest complexity algorithm.

articleTitle: Best rotated cubic lattice constellations for the Rayleigh fading channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we present new algebraic codes for the Rayleigh fading channel. They consist in rotated cubic lattice constellations with full diversity in small dimensions. Based on the minimum product distance, a relevant performance parameter, they appear to be better than all the previously known constructions.

articleTitle: On the rank distance of cyclic codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We study the rank-distance of primitive length (n=q/sup m/-1) linear cyclic codes over F/sub q//sup m/ using the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) description of these codes.

articleTitle: High-rate, full-diversity STBCs from field extensions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A construction of high-rate codes is presented from field extensions that are full-rank also. Also, we discuss the coding gain and decoding of these codes.

articleTitle: On the role of puncturing in hybrid ARQ schemes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In mobile packet data transmission, a special coding/retransmission scheme, known as the type-II hybrid-ARQ (HARQ), achieves higher throughput efficiency then fixed rate codes by adapting their rate to fluctuating channel conditions characteristic for this application. Codes of different rates are obtained by puncturing a chosen low-rate "mother" code. We introduce the notion of random puncturing as a tool to evaluate the performance of punctured codes averaged over a class of puncturing patterns. We illustrate the power of this tool by comparing the throughput performance of an HARQ scheme based on optimized rate compatible puncturing with the throughput performance of an HARQ scheme based on random rate compatible puncturing of the same mother turbo code.

articleTitle: Efficient near-ml decoding via statistical pruning
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On list decoding of alternant codes in the hamming and lee metrics
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Error exponents for watermarking game with squared-error constraints
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we consider an error-exponent game for the following two popular systems: spread-spectrum (SS) watermarking with nearest-neighbor decoding, and quantization-index-modulation (QIM) watermarking with lattice decoding.

articleTitle: Union bound of space-time block codes and decomposable error patterns
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper proposes a single performance index based on union bound analysis on SER at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for space-time modulation design. This union bound approach is extended to the low SNR scenario, where the union bound is expurgated via the use of indecomposable error matrices. Properties of the resultant code sets are summarized.

articleTitle: Concatenated codes for deletion channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On integer codes capable of correcting single errors in two-dimensional lattices
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A special class of linear codes, capable of correcting single errors in a two-dimensional lattice, is introduced. The codes, termed integer codes, are defined over integer rings and are capable of correcting single errors in a lattice with Manhattan distance 1. Three constructions are presented that specify perfect and optimal integer codes for a wide range of parameters, and the corresponding coding algorithms are given.

articleTitle: On the equivalence between scarce-state-transition viterbi decoding and syndrome decoding of convolutional codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Antenna selection for multiple-antenna transmission systems: performance analysis and code construction
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Multiantenna systems employing space-time coding over quasistatic Rayleigh fading channels is considered. We prove that by selecting a subset of the antennas that observe the largest instantaneous signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) at the receiver one can achieve the same diversity order as the full complexity system, provided that the subchannels are independent and the underlying space-time code has full spatial diversity.

articleTitle: On the power efficiency of sensory and ad-hoc wireless networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the power efficiency of a communications channel, i.e., the maximum bit rate that can be achieved per unit power (energy rate). For AWGN channels, it is well known that power efficiency is attained in the low SNR regime. In this paper we show that for a random sensory, or ad-hoc, wireless network with n users (nodes), with high probability converging to one as n grows, the power efficiency scales at least by a factor of /spl radic/n. In other words, each user in a wireless channel with n nodes can support the same communications rate as a single user system, but by expending only 1//spl radic/n the energy.

articleTitle: Implicit and explicit receiver training in flat fading channels modeled as finite state Markov processes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We study the effect of training method on the receiver bit error rate (BER) performance in constant envelope phase modulation schemes that are transmitted through flat fading channels. Here we propose a novel method for receiver training by sending information bits with unbalanced probabilities. We call this method implicit training and compare it with traditional (explicit) training scheme in which known periodic training sequences are sent to the receiver. The simulation results show superior performance of implicit training where the gain is 2 dB at information rate of 0.15 bits/channel use.

articleTitle: Semidefinite methods for approximate inference on graphs with cycles
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Characterizing optimum (input, output) processes for finite-state channels with feedback
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We treat a finite-state channel whose state is the most recent channel output. Markovian characterizations of mutual-information-rate-maximizing constrained (input, output) processes are derived. The study was motivated by a mathematical model of brain function which is briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Iterative least-squares decoding of analog product codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We prove that a turbo-like iterative decoding of an analog product code with parity-check component codes lead to the least-squares solution.

articleTitle: On the university of grammar-based codes for sources with countably infinite alphabets
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Grammar-based codes refer to a new class of universal lossless data compression algorithms. Originally, grammar-based codes were designed and analyzed for sources with finite alphabets. Grammar-based codes are very efficient in many applications like lossless audio compression and high-quality image compression, where data sequences to be compressed are often from large alphabets with cardinalities even comparable to the sequence lengths. In these cases, the assumption of a finite alphabet is hardly justified; instead, one may simply assume that data sequences come from a countably infinite alphabet. This paper investigates the universality and redundancy of grammar-based codes for sources with a countably infinite alphabet.

articleTitle: Capacity analysis of correlated mimo channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Kolynogorov's structure functions, nonprobabilistic statistics, and the foundations of model selection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the burst error detecting and erasure correcting capabilities of convolutional codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper it is shown how a convolutional code can be used either to detect errors or to correct erasures. The erasure correction is related to the error detection. Using the active burst distance lower bounds on the error and erasure correction as well as error detection are obtained for convolutional codes.

articleTitle: Extending MacWilliams identities to the spherical orbit codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: It is well known that MacWilliams identities have numerous applications in the coding theory. Sidelnikov (Ref. 2) proposed an extension of MacWilliams identities to a certain class of orbit group codes. Our aim is to generalize this results to a larger class of groups.

articleTitle: Petri nets compressibility and capacity of concurrent systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the design of nonsystematic turbo codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We address the design of nonsystematic turbo codes and compare their performance with classical systematic turbo codes. We identify some classes of nonsystematic encoders with good convergence properties that make them attractive for se in nonsystematic turbo coding schemes.

articleTitle: On the cost function and splitting criteria in deterministic annealing for the design of entropy constrained vector quantizers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Deterministic annealing is a technique, which has the potential to solve two problems in variable-rate vector quantizer design-avoiding local optima, and determining optimal codebook size and also generalize existing work on the subject to gain insight to proper cost functions and splitting algorithms.

articleTitle: Wavelet estimation of cyclospectra the case of unknown cyclic frequency
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Optimal soft decoding for joint trellis-coded quantization/continuous phase modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The performance of joint trellis coded quantization/continuous phase modulation (TCQ/CPM) has been investigated. The optimal soft decoding algorithm for the combined TCQ/CPM scheme has been derived and the simulation results show that a large improvement can be achieved when compared with hard decoding. The signal to quantization noise ratio performance for the serially concatenated TCQ CPM system with iterative decoding has also been studied. Numerical results indicate that substantial improvement of performance owing to optimal TCQ based on CPM can be achieved at moderate to high signal to noise ratio on an additive white Gaussian noise channel for a memoryless Gaussian source.

articleTitle: Mdl selection criteria for generalized linear models
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Source coding for general penalties
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Redundancy of universal coding, Kolmogorov complexity, and Hausdorff dimension
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The code-lengths shown in this paper give a nontrivial upper and lower bound of Kolmogorov complexity when the source is not a computable measure.

articleTitle: A c-identifying residue-pair representation: sufficient conditions and application to c-secure crt code
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Capacity and spectral efficiency in wideband correlated mimo channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On a decoding algorithm for LDPC codes based on the concave-convex procedure
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we empirically show the effectiveness of double-loop algorithm based on the concave-convex procedure in decoding linear codes.

articleTitle: Optimal two-level q-ary unequal error control codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Chip-based joint processing antenna diversity and equalizer for ds-cdma packet mobile communication systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Nested trellis codes and shaping for the transmitter side-information problem
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we specifically focus on the problem of power shaping and we examine nested constructions based on trellis codes, which build on simple low dimensional lattices. We propose the idea of performing shaping through a coarse lattice (source code) and we also show how this method can actually be combined with shaping through a fine lattice (channel code) so that a joint shaping can be performed by the fine and coarse lattices in the communication channel with transmitter side-information simultaneously.

articleTitle: On reverse concatenation and the rate of average intersection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: It is shown via a combinatorial approach that an infinite cascade of reverse concatenation with independent decoding of the error control code (ECC) and constraint yields a capacity equal to the rate of average intersection.

articleTitle: Highly nonlinear s-boxes with reduced bound on maximum correlation (extended abstract)
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Generalized constellations with low crest-factor for OFDM
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Lowering the crest-factor (CF) in OFDM transmission is still an on-going research topic. Here, we provide a systematic approach for designing point sets in N-space (corresponding to the number of subcarriers in OFDM) with low CF that we call generalized constellations. In order to design codes that have both low CF and high diversity we propose a scheme based on properties of polynomials constituting the class of the so-called de la Vallee-Poussin kernels. The main idea is to use good codes that have small discrete-time crest-factor (for example trace codes) and to apply the interpolation.

articleTitle: A generalization of the Lee distance and error correcting codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We will define an l-dimensional Lee distance, and construct 2-error correcting codes for this distance. The ordinary Lee distance is just the 1-dimensional Lee distance.

articleTitle: The mitigation of mai for ook-cdma systems with optical hard-limiter by transmitting optical pulses with multiple intensities
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Multiantenna capacity in interference-limited low-power conditions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper provides an analytical characterization of the multiantenna capacity for scenarios where the noise is dominated by out-of-cell interference, spatially colored and subject to fading. The analysis is carried out in the region of energy per bit close to its minimum value.

articleTitle: Intuitional decoding algorithm in RAID architecture based on dual parity placement scheme
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper proposes an improved and intuitional dual parity placement scheme, the HD (Horizontal-Diagonal) scheme, to enhance the reliability of a disk array system.

articleTitle: System theoretic approach to geometrically uniform maps
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper we generalize the concept of bit geometrically uniform map and then the system theoretic properties of this class of maps are investigated. By restricting to a particular class of encoders, called bit geometrically uniform encoders, the performance analysis becomes much easier.

articleTitle: Mac layer wireless multicast: theory and approaches
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Precoders for message-passing detection of partial-response channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Parallel message-passing detectors for partial-response channels have the property that a bit is estimated using channel symbols in a window of size W centered upon that bit. Distinct input sequences that produce the same output sequence result in undesirable failure of window decoders, but preceding can eliminate this input-to-output mapping ambiguity. For a class of partial-response channels, we show necessary and sufficient conditions on a precoder to unambiguously map input sequences to output sequences.

articleTitle: Symbol-intersecting codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes an intersecting coding scheme (/spl epsiv/ : M/spl rarr/ (F/sup 2m-1/)/sup n/, D/sub 1/, D/sub 2/) where /spl epsiv/ is an encoding function and D1 and D2 are decoding functions. This paper shows that its application to broadcast channels and it can be verified that users will always be able to recover the transmitted messages if and only if there exists an intersecting coding scheme. An explicit code construction and systematic encoding procedures are also discussed.

articleTitle: Coding combinatorial sources with costs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper we define a combinatorial source by constructing an encoding method with costs and proving its optimality via Kraft's inequality.

articleTitle: Geometric programming dual of channel capacity
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo distance spectrum method for estimating BER of turbo codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A method for estimating the bit-error rate (BER) of turbo codes called the Monte Carlo distance spectrum method is proposed. Testing this method shows that the estimated BER curves closely approximate the results of a Monte Carlo simulation alone for a wide range of signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: Convolutional codes for peak-to-average power ratio reduction in OFDM
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: One of the disadvantages of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems is that OFDM signals may have high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Almost all the previously proposed coding approaches dealing with this problem employ block codes. In this paper, we propose terminated convolutional codes with offset for PAPR reduction. The constructed convolutional codes, which can be easily decoded by using the Viterbi algorithm, have low PAPR and acceptable code rates.

articleTitle: Turbo-like space time coding for beamforming arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we propose and investigate a beam-space time turbo-like coding utilizing the overlap between transmit beams. Since the proposed system resembles partial response coding technique, it can achieve higher coding gain than beam-space time coding systems without overlap. This scheme is a concatenation of a space-time trellis coding and an overlap beam-space time PR coding.

articleTitle: A serial-in-serial-out hardware architecture for systematic encoding of hermitian codes via grobner bases
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Speedup of data access using error correcting codes in peer-to-peer networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Peer-to-peer networks are networks of heterogeneous computers sharing flies or services. This paper proposes to use a data storage scheme using maximum distance separable codes to optimize the dissemination of the data in the network in order to globally enhance the data access.

articleTitle: Lossless image compression using context-dependent multilevel 2D pattern matching
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this study, we will generalize the 1D multilevel pattern matching (MPM) code to 2D data, and analyze the compression performance of the 2D MPM code for lossless image compression. We then extend the 2D MPM code to the case of context modelling, yielding a context-dependent 2D MPM code. Its performance will be theoretically analyzed and experimentally evaluated.

articleTitle: Probability of error for the fixed-length lossy coding of general sources
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Combined modulation/parity codes for magnetic recording
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Inner coding schemes for magnetic recording that cascade a modulation encoder with a parity-check encoder followed by a precoder are considered. A set of desired parity-check equations that are satisfied by the combined modulation/parity code words at the output of the precoder is transformed into a set of parity-check equations at the input of the precoder. Efficient combination of a maximum transition run (MTR) code with a parity-check code is demonstrated by constructing a rate-96/104 combined MTR/parity code that largely retains the properties of the original MTR code.

articleTitle: On block length as delay on real-time communication
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: More on the reliability function of the BSC
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: An improved upper bound is given for the maximum attainable exponent of the error probability of max-likelihood decoding on a binary symmetric channel (the reliability function of the channel).

articleTitle: Clustering by compression
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Lower bound on BER performance of finite length turbo codes using Gaussian approximation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method to obtain the lower bound on the average BER of the finite-length turbo codes in an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel considering the transition probability of the average BER curve between two asymptotes. For this purpose, we use the SNR TCB chart based on the Gaussian approximation of extrinsic values for each frame.

articleTitle: Limits on transmission rates over channels received from middleton's impulsive noise model
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Filter bank frame expansions as joint source-channel codes for robustness to erasures
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper studies oversampled filter banks (OFBs) for robust transmission of multimedia signals over erasure channels. OFBs implement frame expansions, which is an overcomplete expansion of the signal. The 2-channel orthonormal OFB provides a representation of the signal using two orthonormal basis functions. In the event of erasures, conditions under which it is possible to reconstruct the erased values from the received data are studied. This study paves way for message reconstruction in the presence of erasures and quantization noise. Conditions for recovery from some typical erasure patterns like bursty erasures are obtained. We prove that it is not possible to obtain perfect reconstruction if a burst of consecutive erasures of length more than 2 times the filter length occurs.

articleTitle: New family of p-ary sequences with optimal correlation property and large linear span
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: For an odd prime p and an integer n=(2m+1)k, a new family of p-ary sequences with optimal correlation property is constructed using Helleseth-Gong sequences. Period of the sequences is p/sup n/-1 and the size of family is p/sup n/. It is also derived that the linear span of the sequences in the family is (m+2)/spl middot/n except the m-sequence in the family. The maximum nontrivial correlation value R/sub max/ does not exceed 1+/spl radic/(P/sup n/) which means the optimal correlation property in terms of Welch's lower bound.

articleTitle: Extremal distributions, entropy minimization and their application to admission control
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Error exponents of codings for stationary gaussian channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Affine invariant extended cyclic codes over Galois rings
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Affine invariant extended cyclic codes of length p/sup m/ over any subring of GR(p/sup e/,m) for e=2 with arbitrary p and for p=2 with arbitrary e are characterized using transform technique. New classes of affine invariant BCH and GRM codes over such rings are found.

articleTitle: On error exponents in quantum hypothesis testing
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: On error exponents in the simple quantum hypothesis testing problem, a noncommutative analogue of the Hoeffding bound (W. Hoeffding, 1991) is presented. If the hypotheses, namely two density operators, are mutually commutative, the bound is identical with the classical counter part and thus is optimal. As a by-product, a simple proof of the direct part of the quantum Stein's lemma [F. Hiai (1991)] [T. Ogawa (2000)] is also given.

articleTitle: Sequential MPM coding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Two sequential multilevel pattern matching coding schemes (SMPM-1 and SMPM-2) are proposed, which are a kind of dictionary coding method. The SMPM-1 can attain theoretically the maximal redundancy O(1/log n) for any finite state source while the SMPM-2 can attain better compression than the original MPM code and the SMPM-1 for corpora.

articleTitle: Concavity of the second law of thermodynamics
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The second law of thermodynamics states that entropy increases. We interpret this as a physical statement and as an information theoretic statement. We ask to what extent the increase of entropy is built into stochastic processes independently of the physics. Does the increase of entropy provide an arrow of time? What are the assumptions behind Boltzmann's famous H theorem (proving entropy increase) and the quantum version? Do the proofs of the H theorem rely on physical assumptions that imply Markovity or stationarity?.

articleTitle: A new class of pseudonoise sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Set decoding of convolutional codes with application to gsm/gprs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On capacity-achieving sequences of degree distributions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Suboptimal MMSE multiuser receiver design for DS-CDMA multirate systems using spectral correlations
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A new expression for the MMSE (minimum mean-square error) linear receiver is derived in this article for a multirate system using spectral correlation between cycle frequencies and, based it, propose a new design method for the "best" suboptimal linear receiver which requires only the knowledge of bit rates in the system. Computer simulation reveals that it is an efficient design method.

articleTitle: The multicovering radii of linear codes with 1-covering radius one
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The multicovering radius is a generalization of the covering radius that was proposed by Klapper (1997) in the course of studying stream ciphers. Klapper showed that there exist stream ciphers that are resistant to synthesis attacks. The purpose of this paper is to determine the 2-covering radius of linear codes with 1-covering radius one. A technique for determining multicovering radii is illustrated and has generated a new bound.

articleTitle: Universally attainable error-exponents for rate-distortion of noisy sources
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Consider the problem of rate-constrained reconstruction of a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless signal X/sub n/ = (X/sub 1/, ..., X/sub n/), based on a noise-corrupted observation sequence Z/sub n/, which is the finite-alphabet output of a discrete memoryless channel (DMC) whose input is X/sub n/. In this paper universally attainable error-exponents for rate-distortion of noisy sources are given.

articleTitle: Error correction and security in quantum cryptography
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The deep connection between quantum error correction and the security of quantum key distribution has recently been demonstrated. The author survey some results in this subject.

articleTitle: Embedded turbo coding in pattern position modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A novel coded modulation system where turbo coding is embedded in pattern position modulation (PPM) is proposed. We also discuss on the noise model and show performance can be improved by applying a proper discrete interference model.

articleTitle: Trace representation of binary e-th residue sequences of period p
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the wire-tap channel of type II with side information
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Asymptotic two-stage multidimensional quantizer
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the design of two-stage quantiser. By studying a geometry in a distribution space, the second stage quantiser as a combination of a compander and a lattice quantiser is designed. A new compander called a geodesic compander is also proposed and a partial differential equation is also presented.

articleTitle: Uniform power allocation in mimo channels: a came-theoretic approach
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the separation of demodulation and decoding for communications over multiple-antenna channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper studies the property of space time spreading matrices for communications over multiple-antenna channel. We find necessary and sufficient conditions on space time spreading matrices for the separation of demodulation and decoding at the receiver without loss of optimality.

articleTitle: On bandwidth-efficient convolutional ldpc codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Performance improvement with increasing interleaver length for serially concatenated trellis coded modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper shows new results on the dependency of the performance on the interleaver size for multilevel serially concatenated trellis coded modulation. The dependency of bit error rate on interleaver size for multilevel SCTCM and optimum code are also discussed.

articleTitle: Performance of certain receiver interfaces for space-time coded mimo fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the stability of frequency-hop packet radio networks with coding and retransmission backoff
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the stability problem in frequency-hopping (FH) networks. This paper proposes a retransmission strategy to resolve the traffic congestion and error control coding to increase the success probability of packet transmission. This paper suggest that, in order to construct a stable network with maximum throughput, good error control method and retransmission backoff policy are both necessary.

articleTitle: Correlation distribution of quaternary sequences obtained from modified binary gold sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Trellis module for information-theoretic sensitivity analysis of des
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Throughput of nonbinary type-II hybrid ARQ with adaptive modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Hybrid automatic-repeat-request (ARQ) combines the advantages of ARQ and forward-error-control (FEC), and can achieve good throughput with very low bit error rate (BER). In this paper, nonbinary HARQ is proposed and analyzed in terms of throughput. In nonbinary HARQ, half rate shortened Reed-Solomon (RS) code is used in the FEC subsystem instead of binary BCH codes. Nonbinary HARQ is also applied in a cell with adaptive modulation and the average throughput is obtained.

articleTitle: On trellis complexity constrained convolutional codes of maximum length
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The Burrows Wheeler transform asymptotically conserves the Ziv-entropy of almost every sequence from an ergodic source
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we study theoretically the asymptotic property of the Burrows Wheeler transform (BWT) as the block length n/spl rarr//spl infin/, and prove that under an appropriate definition it conserves the Ziv-entropy almost surely. Also we prove that the similar result holds for the case where the move-to-front (MTF) scheme is combined with the BWT.

articleTitle: Near-optimal linear space-time constellations
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Optimal frame synchronization property of pilot bit pattern in compressed mode
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper shows the frame synchronization word (FSW) of pilot bit pattern in 3GPP (3/sup rd/ generation partnership project) W-CDMA (wideband code division multiple access) system are designed to have optimal frame synchronization property in compressed mode using complementary relationship between preferred pair of FSWs.

articleTitle: On the security of yet another reduced version of 3-pass HAVAL
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we find collisions for the first and third passes of 3-pass HAVAL (following HAVAL) which is not using the second pass and not successive two passes. To find a collision in HAVAL, we introduce the scheme of S.W.Park et al.

articleTitle: A class of (/spl gamma//spl rho//sup /spl gamma/-1/,/spl rho//sup /spl gamma//,/spl rho/,/spl gamma/,{0,1}) combinatorially designed LDPC codes with application to ISI channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A systematic construction of regular low density parity check (LDPC) codes based on (/spl gamma//spl rho//sup /spl gamma/-1/,/spl rho//sup /spl gamma//,/spl rho/,/spl gamma/,{0,1}) combinatorial designs is investigated. From one particular view point, the proposed codes are "loosened" finite geometry codes where some lines are systematic removed. The loosened design rules offer at least two advantages: a lower decoding complexity and a richer code set. We show that the proposed codes contain a good combination of structure and pseudorandomness, where the former enables low-cost implementation in hardware and the latter ensures reasonable performance by avoiding certain recurrent error patterns (e.g. rectangular error patterns). One possible application for the proposed structured LDPC codes is the digital recording systems. Simulations show that with proper preceding, the proposed codes can perform as well as or slightly better than the random codes. Unlike random codes, the proposed structured LDPC codes can lend themselves to a low-complexity implementation for high-speed applications.

articleTitle: Power-efficient non-coherent space-time constellations
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Secret function sharing schernes and their applications to the oblivious transfer
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Invariance of stationary and ergodic properties of a quantum source under memoryless transformations
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The stationarity and ergodicity of a quantum source are preserved by any trace-preserving completely positive linear map of the tensor product form /spl epsiv//spl ominus//spl epsiv//spl middot//spl middot//spl middot//spl ominus//spl epsiv/, where a copy of /spl epsiv/ acts locally on each spin lattice site. We also establish ergodicity criteria for so called classically-correlated quantum sources.

articleTitle: Graph-theoretic construction of low-density parity-check codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper presents a novel graph-theoretic method for constructing low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes from connected graphs-without the requirement of large girth. The method is based on finding a set of paths in a connected graph, which satisfies the constraint that any two paths in the set are either disjoint or cross each other at one and only one vertex. Two trellis-based algorithms for finding these paths are devised. Good LDPC codes of practical lengths are constructed and they perform well with iterative decoding.

articleTitle: On the achievable rates of ultra-wideband systems in multipath fading environments
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Augmentation and decoding of compound-error-correcting codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A compound error is any combination of burst errors with various burst lengths including random errors. The compound weight of any such error is defined as a kind of combinational metric which is a generalization of Gabidulin's metric. First, we present a fast method for calculating the weight of any word based on a kind of trellis diagram. Extending the two-dimensional trellis diagram to a three-dimensional trellis, we propose a method of constructing codes having higher coding rate by augmenting any compound-error-correcting codes. Furthermore, we propose a decoding method for any such codes by modifying the three-dimensional trellis in augmentation.

articleTitle: Computation efficient multicast key distribution
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we adopt a common model where session keys are issued and distributed by a central group controller (GC). The resources needed for the GC to distribute session keys to group members include communication, storage and computation resources. A new dynamic group key distribution scheme, in which the rekeying process that reduces computation complexity and yet maintain at least the same security degree of using symmetric encryption algorithms is also discussed.

articleTitle: Proceedings 2003 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory. ISIT 2003 (Cat. No.03CH37432)
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: LDPC codes; OFDM; communication theory; coding theory; cryptography; data compression; entropy; constrained codes; Shannon theory; space-time block codes; source coding; multi-antenna systems; space-time codes; coded modulation; rate distortion function; blind equalization; soft-decision decoding; signal processing; pattern recognition; fading channels; MIMO channels; ML and MAP decoding; channel capacity; multiuser detection; convolutional codes; multiple access channels; multiuser channel coding; turbo codes; algebraic codes; CDMA; random number and random sequence; iterative decoding; Gaussian channels; data networks; list decoding; trellis decoding; burst error and erasure correction; quantum information theory; ARQ; image coding; quantization.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Optimum modulo 2/sup m/ multidimensional transform diffusion in block ciphers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A subspace-based active user identification scheme for cdma ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A zero-redundancy estimator for the context tree weighting method with a finite window
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A modification of the finite window context tree weighting (FWCTW) [H. Sakaguti, et al., 1997] lossless data compression algorithm is considered. First, we give an exposition of the basic framework of FWCTW. Next, we propose a zero-redundancy estimator for FWCTW and verify that our estimator, which is computed with finite precision actually encodes and decodes the data sequence.

articleTitle: Multilayered digital watermarking system based on guided scrambling
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper provides a concept on how to embed multiple watermark sequences by using guided scrambling (GS) techniques. The geometrical interpretation of the multilayered watermark embedding is described, and the watermarking algorithm based on the interpretation is also proposed.

articleTitle: On hyperbolic type codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A distributed splitting algorithm for exploiting multiuser diversity
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Importance sampling for loop-free decoding trees with application to low-density parity-check codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: An importance sampling scheme for the decoding of loop-free decoding trees is proposed. It is shown that this scheme is asymptotically efficient and that, for an arbitrary tree and a given estimation precision, the number of simulation runs needed is inversely proportional to the standard deviation of the channel noise. This work has its application to the decoding of low-density parity-check codes.

articleTitle: Constituent code optimization for space-time turbo modulation over fast fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper proposes a design method for constituent recursive space-time trellis codes (Rec-STTrCs) and parallel concatenated space-time turbo coded modulation (STTuCM) as a new framework for building low complexity, large equivalent constraint-length STTrCs. The code distance spectrum optimization over fast fading channels for minimum spectral product criteria are also discussed.

articleTitle: Quasicyclic codes from a finite affine plane
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the properties of the point-line incidence matrix of a finite affine plane and present a construction of quasicyclic LDPC codes based on submatrices of the incidence matrix. The codes from the point-line incidence matrices of the affine and projective geometries perform very well with iterative decoding algorithms for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes.

articleTitle: On the quadratic span of binary sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The channel coding theorem and the security of binary randomization
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A simulation based algorithm for optimal quantization of hidden Markov models
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A general problem of multilevel scalar quantization of hidden Markov models is considered. An algorithm for the optimal selection of the quantization levels is proposed and its asymptotic behavior is analyzed theoretically and through simulations. The proposed algorithm is based on stochastic approximation and Monte Carlo gradient estimation.

articleTitle: On closures of exponential families and their subfamilies
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The variation distance closures of exponential families and their log-convex subfamilies are characterized. A problem left open in (I. Csiszar, et al., 2002) is settled: an exponential family is constructed whose closure in reversed information divergence, rI-closure, is neither rI-closed nor log-convex.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of bit error probability for maximum a posteriori probability decoding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Entropy and the law of small numbers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we give an elementary information theoretic proof of some Poisson approximation inequalities for sums of discrete random variables. These can be thought of as "maximum entropy" statements in that, under suitable conditions, the distribution of the sum converges to the distribution which has "maximal entropy" within an appropriate class. We also outline a general method for obtaining corresponding bounds when approximating the distribution of a sum of general discrete random variables by an infinitely divisible distribution.

articleTitle: Ordered subsets message-passing
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Simple construction of quantum universal variable-length source coding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
