abstract: This paper describes the construction of a quantum universal variable-length source code in which, independent of information source, both of the average error and the probability that the coding rate is greater than the entropy rate H(/spl rho/~/sub p/), tend to 0. If H(/spl rho/~/sub p/) is estimated, and compress the coding rate to the admissible rate H(/spl rho/~/sub p/) with a probability close to 1. However, when we perform a naive measurement for the estimation of H(/spl rho/~/sub p/), the input state is demolished. By smearing the measurement, we successfully treat the trade-off between the estimation of H(/spl rho/~/sub p/) and the nondemolition of the input state. Our protocol can be used not only for the Schumacher's compression but also for the compression of entangled states.

articleTitle: Concatenated codes: serial and parallel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, new construction methods of parallel-concatenated codes that are analogous to more traditional serial concatenations are presented (for instance, Forney's concatenated codes). Improved lower bounds on error exponents attainable under linear-time decoding are established. As the rate approaches the capacity of a binary symmetric channel, these exponents come arbitrarily close to the sphere-packing bound.

articleTitle: Joint erasure marking and viterbi algorithm for detecting impulsive noise corrupted signals
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Asymptotic average redundancy of adaptive block codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Sample-based (or adaptive) block codes represent a transitional case: while the exact parameters of a source are not known, one can obtain finite length sequences of symbols (or samples) produced by this source in the past. It turns out, that using such samples it is possible to construct codes that are more efficient in encoding this particular source than pure universal codes. In order to be able to compare adaptive codes and codes for a known source more precisely one clearly needs to know the exact expression of an O (1/n). Obtaining the exact expression for this and subsequent terms describing the average behavior of adaptive block codes is the main goal of this paper.

articleTitle: Irregular low-density parity-check code design based on integer lattices
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We propose an irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) code design scheme by extension of a regular LDPC code using Latin square matrices of random sequence. Our scheme is a deterministic method that enables to easily design good irregular LDPC code for any code rate and degree distributions. We optimize LDPC codes by Gaussian approximation (GA) Chung, S-Y et al., (2001) method and construct irregular LDPC codes based on integer lattices Vasic, B et al., (2002).

articleTitle: Direct brain-computer communication with user rewarding mechanism
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On partial ordering of markov modulated channels under ldpc decoding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Error probability evaluation with a limited number of moments
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In digital communications systems the error probability can often be expressed as the expectation of a function of an interference random variable. To approximate such expectations a number of methods have been proposed such as series expansion methods, Gauss quadrature rules and maximum entropy and minimum relative entropy methods. The methods proposed to approximate the error probability expectations typically require knowledge of a large number of moments of the interference random variable which may not be always available. In this paper, we use the Pearson system of distributions to approximate the distribution of the interference random variable and we then use the approximate distribution to compute the error probability expectations. This system of distributions has been used in a variety of situations to model distributions whose behaviour deviates from Gaussian behaviour. Very good agreement is observed between the Pearson approximation and simulation in the intersymbol interference case. Very good agreement was also observed between the Pearson approximation and simulation in the intermodulation distortion case.

articleTitle: Bandwidth requirements for protected vpns in the hose model
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: An iterative siso strategy for mimo fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Space-time block codes from designs for fast-fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We study space-time block codes from orthogonal designs (V. Tarokh et al., 1999), (Zafar Ali Khan et al., 2002) for use in fast-fading channels by giving a matrix representation of the multiantenna fast-fading channels.

articleTitle: A coding theorem on the shannon cipher system with a general source using fixed-length homophonic coding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: An information-theoretic analysis of Grover's algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper presents an information-theoretic analysis of Grover's algorithm and give a tight lower bound on the complexity of search algorithms using Grover's oracle. This paper also proposes the square-root speed-up performance gain of a quantum search algorithm and the significance of tight bounds based on Grover's oracle algorithm to identify target element.

articleTitle: The impact of user information on power-delay tradeoffs in bursty packetized systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper explores the power-delay tradeoff for a time-slotted multiple user system with random packet arrivals and limited sharing of user queue information. The average power consumption to minimize delay with full and only local queue information, as well as without regards to delay is analyzed. A simple scheme with one bit of global queue information is presented. The scheme uses superposition coding to afford reliably received in the presence of collisions and can achieve power-delay trade-offs between minimizing energy and minimizing delay.

articleTitle: Lowest-density MDS codes over extension alphabets
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we identify a range of parameters for which the codes Z/sub p/(p,r) are provably maximum distance separable (MDS). This paper presents a definition of the codes Z/sub p/(p,r) and then summarize our results using F/sub q/ to denote the finite field with q elements.

articleTitle: On the redundancy of universal trellis lossy source coding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we construct an adaptive entropy coded trellis lossy source coding coding scheme for memoryless sources. The scheme utilizes a fully connected trellis with a set of fixed-rate state codebooks and adaptive probability mass function for the codewords. Since the usage frequency of each codeword is known at the decoder, no overhead is necessary for adapting the probabilities mass functions of the codebooks. Thus, using recent redundancy result in trellis coding [G.-C. Zhou et al., 2002] and universal random block codes designed in [E.-H. Yang et al., 2001], we show that the proposed coding scheme is universal and its redundancy is also of the form O(1/n), which is the same order as that of trellis source coding with known statistics.

articleTitle: Construction of low density parity check codes from optical orthogonal codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new method for generating low-density parity check codes (LPDC) from optical orthogonal codes (OOC). The parity check matrix of an LDPC code is constructed by selecting the rows of the parity-check matrix from amongst the codewords of an OOC, taking care to include all the cyclic shifts of a codeword when the codeword itself has been selected.

articleTitle: Reduced complexity soft-input soft-output "box and match" decoding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On balanced codes over the m-th roots of unity, m=4
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper completely solves the coding problem for balanced codes over /spl Phi//sub m/, when m = 4. In fact, it reduces the problem of designing efficient coding schemes for balanced codes over /spl Phi//sub 4/ to the design of efficient balanced codes over /spl Phi/4 = {-1,+1}. In particular, the paper proposes efficient constructions for balanced codes over /spl Phi//sub 4/ with k information digits and r=2log/sub 4/k -log/sub 4/s(k) + /spl Theta/(1), check digits, where s(k) is any function such that 1/spl les/s(k)/spl les/k. Such balanced codes can be implemented with T=O(klogk:+ ks(k)) digit operations, by storing A=O(k+s/sup 3/(k)) memory digits. The paper also shows that the minimum redundancy for a balanced code over /spl Phi//sub 4/ of length n is r/sub min/ /spl ap/ Iog/sub 4/n+0.326.

articleTitle: Approach the capacity of multiple access channels using interleaved low rate codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Remarks on concavity of the auxiliary function appearing in quantum reliability function
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Concavity of the auxiliary function which appears in the random coding exponent as the lower bound of the quantum reliability function for general quantum states is proved for 0/spl les/s/spl les/1 in two dimensional case.

articleTitle: Density evolution analysis of correlated sources compressed with LDPC codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We consider a compression system for memory correlated binary sources using irregular LDPC codes as source codes. In order to incorporate the hidden Markov model (HMM) defining the source correlation, we propose a modified density evolution algorithm. Irregular LDPC codes optimized with this algorithm achieve a performance close to the theoretical Slepian-Wolf limit.

articleTitle: Diversity-multiplexing tradeoff for multiaccess channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: App equalization for non-ideal channel knowledge
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Zero-error source-channel coding with source side information at the decoder
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes the zero-error source-channel coding with source side information at the decoder. To analyze the zero-error scenario, we define the following graphs: the source confusability graph G/sub u/ and channel characteristic graph G/sub x/. We can always find a code from a source graph to its complement. Separate source and channel coding corresponds to first mapping from the source alphabet to an index set and then mapping from the index set to the channel alphabet. The size of the smallest index set that allows a zero-error source code is the chromatic number of G/sub u/, /spl chi/(G/sub u/). The largest index set from which we can map to the channel alphabet is the stability number of G/sub x/, /spl alpha/(G/sub x/).

articleTitle: Expectation propagation for signal detection in flat-fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Scalable and efficient multirate data distribution
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we address the rate assignment issue by introducing rate-controlled streams (RCS). A RCS is a data stream encoded from an original source data, with a specific sending rate. We propose a mathematical framework in which multiple RCSs can be combined to form a new RCS with higher rate, deriving conditions for achieving optimal stream-combining in terms of the aggregate rate. We then study how to optimally assign rates to multiple streams which are sent over different channels with possible packet loss to meet rate constraints imposed by receivers.

articleTitle: Uniform scalar quantizers-distortion and the additive noise model
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: High-resolution infinite level uniform scalar quantizers are considered for the two cases when cell midpoints and cell centroids are used as reconstruction levels. First, it is shown that asymptotically, as the cell size goes to zero, midpoints induce the same MSE as centroids. Hence, they are asymptotically MSE optimal. Secondly, sufficient conditions are found under which the commonly used additive noise model, when midpoints are used, is asymptotically correct. It is also shown that for input probability density functions (pdf's) that have a single jump discontinuity not at the origin, such a model is not well defined and consequently incorrect.

articleTitle: Optimal linear multistage receivers with unequal power users
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Trellis shaped coded OFDM systems with high power efficiency
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A new trellis shaping design is proposed for the coded OFDM systems. We derive the branch metric based on the autocorrelation of transmit sequence. By minimizing the sidelobe components of the autocorrelation, the proposed trellis shaping can reduce both peak-to-average power ratio and average power of the band-limited QAM-OFDM signals. Computational reduction for metric calculation is also proposed.

articleTitle: Analysis of multiple antenna wireless links at low SNR
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In the low signal-to-noise (SNR) regime when the channel is not known to both transmitter and receiver, we show that the capacity of a multiple antenna Rayleigh fading link is asymptotically quadratic in the SNR for all practical input distributions. This is much less than the known channel case where it exhibits a linear growth in the SNR. Under various signaling constraints we show that mutual information is maximized by using a single transmit antenna. Also sending training symbols offers no advantage at low SNR.

articleTitle: Adaptive channel coding scheme using finite state machine
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a coding and decoding scheme to achieve adaptive channel coding using a finite state machine (FSM). Adaptive channel coding and decoding systems that can switch between different coding rates and error correcting capabilities in order to adapt to changing applications and environments, are effective. However, in these systems, a receiver cannot always select the correct decoder which causes decoding errors, usually referred to as decoder-selection-errors (DSE) (Mari Matsunaga, et al., 1998). We propose a trellis encoder estimation scheme that compensates for this problem. This scheme uses the circuit of FSM to limit the encoder transition and the Viterbi algorithm for maximum likelihood trellis encoder estimation. Computer simulations are applied for evaluating the DSE rate, of the proposed scheme in comparison with a conventional scheme.

articleTitle: The throughput of ldpc-based incremental-redundancy schemes with finite blocklength
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: New lower bounds on the error probability for signals over an AWGN channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: New lower bounds on the error probability when communicating one of M equally likely signals over an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel are proposed. The bounds are derived by improving on a recent lower bound on the probability of a union of events by de Caen, and applying it to this problem. The resulting bounds, specialized for linear codes, improve on the latest lower bound appearing in the current literature by Seguin.

articleTitle: Improved design criteria and new codes for space-frequency trellis coding over frequency selective fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this summary, we propose new design criteria on the coding gain of space-frequency trellis codes (SFTC's) with and without interleaver when the diversity order is moderate. Moreover, we propose new 4-PSK, 4 state and 8-PSK, 8 state SFTC's that achieve good frame error rates (FER's) with and without interleaver by computer search based on the proposed design criteria.

articleTitle: The power spectra of good codes for partial response channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the second-order statistics of the matched information rate code (MIRC) sequence. Recently, a serial concatenation coding scheme was proposed to approach the capacity of a partial response (PR) channel, which is a basic model for digital recording systems. In this paper, we compute the power spectral density (p.s.d.) of the suboptimal binary input process concentrate in the frequency band where the water-filling solution(Gaussian channel) does not vanish and has low-powers(but not zero) at channel spectral nulls.

articleTitle: An instance of multiuser diversity in wireless networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Existing forms of multiuser diversity can be seen as instances of the fundamental economic trade-off of fairness versus efficiency. This viewpoint points to an instance of multiuser diversity which arises in multiuser communication networks. The key idea is to exploit the time-varying buffer occupancies of different users in order to maximize the admissible arrival rate for each user.

articleTitle: Dependent and gaussian erasure networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Covariance shaping multiuser detection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Information rates achievable with algebraic codes on discrete memoryless quantum channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The highest information rate at which quantum error-correction schemes work reliably on a channel, which is called the quantum capacity, is proven to be lower bounded by the limit of the quantity termed coherent information maximized over the set of input density operators which are proportional to the projections onto the code spaces of symplectic (stabilizer) codes. Quantum channels to be considered are those subject to independent errors and modeled as tensor products of copies of a completely positive linear map on a Hilbert space of finite dimension, and the codes that are proven to have the desired performance are symplectic codes. On the depolarizing channel, this work's bound is actually the highest possible rate at which symplectic codes work reliably. The details of this work can be found in (M. Hamada, 2002).

articleTitle: Map detection in noisy channels with synchronization errors (including the insertion/deletion channel)
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Optimality of the natural binary code for quantizers with channel optimized decoders
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, the mean squared error (MSE) for the natural binary code and for randomly chosen index assignments are calculated, and the natural binary code is shown to be mean squared optimal among all possible index assignments.

articleTitle: Approaching the capacity of the mimo rayleigh flat-fading channel with qam constellations, independent across antennas and dimensions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Generalized APP detection for unknown ISI channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Soft information is computed in a simple way. In particular, we investigate iterative detection of serially concatenated continuous phase modulation corrupted by unknown intersymbol interference.

articleTitle: Beamformer design with feedback rate constraints: criteria and constructions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes the design of beamformers when finite rate channel feedback is available in a multiple transmit antenna system. This paper also discusses a geometrical framework for the analysis and design criterion of beamformer codebooks construction with finite number of beam-former vectors to minimize the outage probability.

articleTitle: On the existence of codes with constant bounded PMEPR for multicarrier signals
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: It has been shown that with probability one the peak to mean envelope power ratio (PMEPR) of any random codeword chosen from a symmetric QAM/PSK constellation is log n where n is the number of subcarriers (M. Sharif, et al., 2003). In this paper, the existence of codes with nonzero rate and PMEPR bounded by a constant is established.

articleTitle: Unconditionally secure homomorphic pre-distributed commitments
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Soft-decision decoding of linear block codes using multiple information bases
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Optimal power control for CDMA systems in the wideband limit
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Traditional methods for solving multiuser control problems in CDMA systems do not scale well as the number of users in the system increases. To address this problem we develop a wideband limit approximation for dynamic programming problems in CDMA systems. This approximation greatly simplifies the state space and evolution equations for the users in a CDMA cell, thereby simplifying the optimal control problem. This wideband convergence result holds for a number of different linear multiuser receiver structures including the MMSE and matched filter receivers.

articleTitle: Upper bound on the minimum average cycle weight of classes of convolutional codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Geometrically uniform space-time codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On the weight distribution of Justesen codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we give the weight distributions of Justesen codes obtained by using some other RS codes as the outer code. Justesen first constructed asymptotically good concatenated codes such that the outer code is Reed-Solomon (RS) code and the inner code is Wozencraft's ensemble of randomly shifted codes.

articleTitle: On variable-length coding of sources with side information at multiple decoders
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we generalize Simonyi's result to the case of variable-length coding. Our result shows that the asymptotic minimum rate is given by the maximum complementary graph entropy in the characteristic graph family.

articleTitle: Improved constructions of secret sharing schemes by applying (/spl lambda/,w)-decompositions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Error-correction capability of binary linear codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, the error-correction capability of binary linear codes and the discrete simplex problem is discussed.

articleTitle: Exploiting protocol information for transmission over unknown fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A parallel iterative decoding algorithm for zero-tail and tail-biting convolutional codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the parallel propagation algorithm applied to the decoding of convolutional codes. The parallel algorithm surpasses the BCJR algorithm in parallel computational complexity and performance when it is applied to tail-biting codes. The complexity of iterative decoding algorithms depends on the calculation of posterior probability and bit error probability by using clique and number of iterations. The computational complexity of the parallel algorithm for tail-biting codes is almost the same as that for zero-tail convolutional codes.

articleTitle: Unitary subgroup space-time codes using Bruhat decomposition and Weyl groups
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper is proposed new untiary subgroups for differential space-time codes. The subgroups are constructed on the basis of double coset decomposition, Bruhat decomposition. Also, we give some examples of the proposed subgroup space-time codes, and describe how the new codes are combined with coded modulation systems.

articleTitle: On the Wyner-Ziv problem with two sources
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper studies the rate-distortion region for the Wyner-Ziv problem with two sources having side information. The inner and outer bounds to this region is presented.

articleTitle: Upper bound for the size of monotone span programs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Maximum multipath diversity with linear equalization in linearly precoded OFDM systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper we show that a linear equalizer with no coding is capable of benefiting from maximum multipath diversity in linearly preceded OFDM systems Z. Wang et al., (2001), i.e. systems where the information symbols are mapped through a matrix transformation before the IFFT at the OFDM transmitter. We can conclude from this result that at sufficiently high SNRs precoded OFDM systems perform better over channels with more taps even with linear equalization, due to the increase in diversity order.

articleTitle: Communication near the channel capacity with an absence of compression: statistical mechanical approach
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: An MN-Gallager code over Galois fields, q, based on the dynamical block posterior probabilities (DBF) for messages with a given set of autocorrelations is presented. The novel idea of the decoder is the dynamical updating of the prior block probabilities which are derived from the transfer matrix solution of the effective ID Ising Hamiltonian and from the posterior probabilities of the neighboring blocks. This bridge between statistical physics and information theory leads to an efficient algorithm for joint source-channel coding.

articleTitle: Trellis decoding of permutation modulations
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Cascading constrained 2-D arrays using periodic merging arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We consider a method for designing 2-D constrained codes by cascading finite width arrays using predefined finite width periodic merging arrays. This provides a constructive lower bound on the capacity of the 2-D constrained code. Examples include symmetric RLL and density constrained codes. Numerical results for the capacities are presented.

articleTitle: Stabilization of block-type-decodability properties for constrained systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper aims to compute the optimal code rate for each class of encoder and an achieving set of principal states. We are interested in two cases: finite and asymptotically large codeword lengths. A relationship between the two cases will be presented. We consider block-type-decodable encoders which comprise: block (blk), block-decodable (blkdec), and deterministic (det) encoders.

articleTitle: Towards characterizing the nonlocality of entangled quantum states
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We propose a so-called pseudo-telepathy game for n players demonstrating the nonlocality of quantum information. The simplicity of its classical analysis contrasts the often quite involved analysis of previously proposed such games (G. Brassard, 1999). Moreover, our game allows for a quantitative characterization of entanglement in terms of communication complexity.

articleTitle: Chip-level detector with optimum comparator threshold and correlation receiver with an electrical hard-limiter for optical cdma
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Nonparametric regression estimation by normalized radial basis function networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: An alternative approach to constructing the minimal trellis for linear block codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Conversion of a general quantum stabilizer code to an entanglement distillation protocol
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We show how to convert a quantum stabilizer code to a one-way or two-way entanglement distillation protocol, and give an example of a converted two-way protocol better than the recurrence protocol and the quantum privacy amplification protocol.

articleTitle: On the trade-off between performance and rate for finite alphabet mimo systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Perfect sequences of length 3p
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: New classes of perfect sequences of length 3p, where p is a prime, are proposed. An explicit construction is given for p/spl equiv/3 mod 4.

articleTitle: On asymmetric error detection performance
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A lower bound for the detected error probability for systematic asymmetric error detecting (AED) codes is introduced, using the Z-channel model. This bound finds applicability in evaluating any feedback control system for asymmetric transmission channels.

articleTitle: On coded modulation based on finite rings of integers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem how to use codes over /spl Zopf//sub A/ to correct any single error which belongs to the set {/spl plusmn/e/sub 1/,/spl plusmn/e/sub 2/,...,/spl plusmn/e/sub s/}, where e/sub i/'s are different elements in /spl Zopf//sub A/. We present some classes of such codes and describe how they can be applied to M-QAM.

articleTitle: On the application of a ldpc codes to arbitrary discrete-memoryless channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Higher order asymptotics of mutual information for nonlinear channels with nongaussian noise
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we are interested in finding the higher order asymptotics of the mutual information I(X; /spl epsi/f(X) + Z] up to terms of order o(/spl epsi//sup n/) as /spl epsi/ /spl rarr/ 0 where n is a given integer, n /spl ges/ 2. The higher order asymptotics for such mutual information in the simplest channel model V. V. Prelov (1989) was found in V. V. Prelov (1988) for the case where the noise Z is Gaussian and in V. V. Prelov (1989) if Z is nonGaussian. In the recent paper V. V. Prelov, S. Verdu (2002), the second order asymptotics of the mutual information was found for multidimensional complex-valued nonlinear channels similar to V. V. Prelov (1988) with a Gaussian noise Z.

articleTitle: Consta-abelian codes over galois rings in the dft domain
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A generalized decomposition approach to multi-h continuous phase modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A decomposition approach to continuous phase modulation (CPM), mostly due to the work of Rimoldi (1988), is significant in the design of combined coding and communication signaling scheme. In this paper the generalized decomposition model is developed and applies to the multi-h CPM. It is shown that any multi-h CPM can also be realized by a continuous phase encoder (CPE) concatenated with a memoryless modulator (MM). Moreover, depending on the manner that the modulation indexes are selected for each symbol interval, the CPE can be either a linear or nonlinear feedback convolutional encoder, in which both the CPE and MM are time-variant. Finally, some applications are employed to verify the advantage of the proposed decomposition model, namely, (1) natural trellis representation of the CPE for M-ary single-h CPM with different modulation indexes that have the same denominator P, (2) a reduction of the number of states of the MLSD receiver for conventional multi-h CPM, (3) asymmetrical multi-h CPM has no gain over conventional multi-h CPM, (4) nonlinear CPM has a CPE that is nonlinear.

articleTitle: Base station assignment and power control algorithms for data users in a wireless multiaccess fyamework
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The ML decoding performance of LDPC ensembles over /spl Zopf//sub q/
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this work we derive the asymptotic spectrum of two ensembles of q-ary LDPC codes, one consisting of (almost entirely) binary matrices, the other of q-ary matrices, and show that both ensembles are good as the graph connectivity increases, in the sense that their spectrum approaches that of the random linear ensemble over /spl Zopf//sub q/ and that they allow to approach the random coding error exponent of modulo additive noise channels. This suggests that q-ary LDPC codes may conceivably provide an alternative to multilevel binary LDPC codes for the AWGN channel.

articleTitle: On some singularities in parameter estimation problems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Fully-diverse sp(2) code design
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Distance properties of irregular LDPC codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the distance properties of irregular LDPC codes using the ensemble construction proposed by Richardson et al (Ref. 2). By generalizing the method introduced by Gallager for regular LDPC codes [R.G. Gallager, 1963], we calculate the average weight distribution of irregular LDPC codes. Then, we interpret the stability condition of density evolution as a sufficient condition so that the error probability due to low weight codewords tends to zero under maximum-likelihood decoding.

articleTitle: An implementation of public key cryptosystem TTM with linear time complexity for decryption
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: T. Moh invented a cryptosystem called tame transformation method (TTM). TTM cryptosystem is claimed to be the fastest among all currently known unbroken public key cryptosystems. We have done an actual implementation with linear time complexity for decryption and made some performance tests on it to verify the claim of speed. Also, we give some discussion on our TTM implementation and some attacks on TTM.

articleTitle: On the extreme cases of the rate-distortion function for robust descriptions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A multiterminal source coding scenario known as robust descriptions coding, where the source is to be encoded in a way that enables good descriptions for several distortion measures simultaneously is considered. Our result is obtained by posing robust descriptions as a special case of successive refinement coding.

articleTitle: A new statistical testing for random numbers and its application to some cryptographic problems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Blind detection of OFDM signals in fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we apply branch and bound principle to solve the equivalent nonlinear integer programming problem. A recursive formula for fast metric update is obtained by exploiting the intrinsic characteristics of our objective function. The impacts of reordering the data sequence and selective detection are addressed. By suggesting a preferred order and selective detection method, we greatly reduce the detector complexity while giving up little performance loss. We also extend our investigation to the semiblind case where only sparse pilot symbols are available.

articleTitle: On binary linear [160,80,24] codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper discusses the construction of binary linear Golay [160, 80] (mn,mk) codes from an extended Reed Solomon [32, 16] (n, k) code over F/sub 32/ (F/sub 2//sup m/) by concatenating the given code with a suitable basis symmetric representation of Frobenius automorphism F/sub 32/ over F/sub 2/ with a minimum distance 24.

articleTitle: On achievable key rates for universal simulation of random data with respect to a set of statistical tests
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: j-rotation space time block codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The so-called j-rotation space time block codes (j-STBC) to achieve additional coding gain from correlations of the quasiorthogonal designs is described in this paper.

articleTitle: Iterative decoding of dual-k convolutional codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A new interval source coding scheme over an ordered alphabet
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we propose an intermediate between the MTF and interval source coding schemes, which makes explicit use of alphabetical ordering as well as of symbol frequencies. The proposed scheme encodes the number of symbols that have appeared since the last previous occurrence of the current symbol, but counts only those symbols that are alphabetically bigger than the current symbol. The proposed method is capable of removing data redundancy due to symbols occurrence order.

articleTitle: Joint transmitter and receiver optimization for PAM in additive cyclostationary noise
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: One of the classical problems in communication theory is the problem of jointly optimizing transmitter and receiver waveforms. In this paper, the solution to the joint optimization with the noise modeled as a wide-sense cyclostationary (WSCS) sequence random process with the period of cyclostationarity same as the inverse of the symbol rate. This joint optimization technique for single user channel is of recent interest because it can be applied to iteratively solve the MIMO joint optimization problem. It is worth noting that this scenario includes code-division multiple-access communications over frequency selective channels.

articleTitle: The impact of service rate fluctuations in wireless packet data systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Following a model similar to that of Telatar and Gallager, multiuser communication systems with a varying number of users are studied. It is shown that fading causes variability in the service process, and reduces the effective service rate seen by a user. This result is used to design a power control scheme that balances the twin goals of low service variability and high mean service rate.

articleTitle: New trellis source codes based on linear congruential recursions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We evaluate new rate-distortion codes based on simple linear congruential recursions. Codes are demonstrated for the uniform and Gaussian sources and their performance exceeds that so far reported in the literature, including TCQ.

articleTitle: On the achievable rate/diversity for CPM MIMO fading channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper presents the rate and diversity trade-off for CPM MIMO block fading channels. How to design space-time codes to achieve the optimal trade-off is also given.

articleTitle: Transmission of bursty data over wideband fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the problem of transmitting bursty, delay-sensitive data over time-varying channels is an important issue in next-generation wireless networks. There is a fundamental tradeoff of conserving a mobile user's energy while providing a desired level of quality of service. We present the first known results in this context for fading channels with infinite bandwidth and investigate the tradeoff between average packet delay and average power consumption.

articleTitle: Channel coding algorithm simulating the random coding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: On cycle-based permutor designs for serially concatenated convolutional codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Open-loop transmit diversity of downlink CDMA systems over Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes the transmit diversity for a downlink multiuser CDMA system with distinct signature waveforms assigned to distinct antennas. We derive an upper bound of error probability and propose a new class of signature waveforms with which we can achieve the same BER as a system with orthogonal spread sequences for the number of user near to the processing gain. The proposal system is simple to implement and allows a simple receiver.

articleTitle: Unitary alamouti code design from apsk signals with fast maximum-likelihoo'd decoding algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The asymptotic capacity of multidimensional runlength-limited constraints and independent sets in hypergraphs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Let C(n,d) be the Shannon capacity of the n-dimensional (d,/spl infin/)-runlength-limited (RLL) constraint. We show that lim/sub n/spl rarr//spl infin//C(n,d)=1/(d+1).

articleTitle: Words of minimal weight and weight distribution of binary Goppa codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Little is known about the weight distribution of binary Goppa codes, however it is sure that it is close to a binomial distribution [F. Levy-dit-Vehel, et al., 1997]. That is, the number of words of weight w in a code of length n is approximately (/sub n//sup w/)/spl times/2/sup k-n/. This is true when w is not too small, but when w is close to 0 the distribution is not the same: for instance, for any weight from 1 to 2t the number of words is 0. Using an algorithm to find words of minimal weight we were able to perform some statistics on the small weights distribution and show that even for weights close to the minimal weight bound, the distribution is still binomial-like.

articleTitle: Codecell convexity in optimal entropy-constrained vector quantization
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Properties of optimal entropy-constrained vector quantizers (ECVQs) are studied for the mean squared error (MSB) distortion measure. It is known that restricting an ECVQ to have convex codecells may preclude its optimality for some sources with discrete distribution and show that for sources with continuous distribution, any finite-level ECVQ can be replaced by another finite-level ECVQ with convex codecells that has equal or better performance. This paper also considers the problem of existence of optimal ECVQs for continuous source distributions.

articleTitle: The error distribution of linear block codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper gives an approximate formula to compute the error spectrum of linear block codes and the relationship between the distribution of errors and the input-redundancy weight enumerating function (IRWEF) of the codes is examined. Numerical results confirm that the given expression is a promising tool to analyze the error distribution of linear block codes. For binary zero tail terminated convolutional codes and block turbo codes, the error spectrum is computed as an explicit function of the block length.

articleTitle: Capacity of an OFDM spatial multiplexing system in presence of realistic channel delay profiles
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Classically, channel delay profiles are simplified in order to make simulations easier, so that the effect of bandlimiting filters is not taken into account. Here, we provide a careful analysis of the consequences of this simplification, and compare the deterministic and ergodic capacities, as well as outage probability in the original and simplified cases. It is shown that such simplifications should be used with great care, since, for example, the outage capacity can be somewhat different in both cases.

articleTitle: Band edges pairing for minimum rate sampling
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Packet based unequal error-protection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A new design for space-time multiple trellis codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In ST-MTCM, the inter-distance, especially the intra-distance can determine the system performance, therefore, we focus attention on maximizing the intra-distance and the inter-distance. Using the proposed scheme, the optimum codes can achieve the theoretical maximal diversity gain and improves the coding gain compared to known codes.

articleTitle: A design of 2 by 2 unitary space-time codes from sphere packing theory with optimal diversity product of code size 6
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we propose some designs of 2/spl times/2 unitary space-time codes by using sphere packing theory. In particular, we present an optimal 2/spl times/2 unitary space-time code of size 6 in the sense that it reaches the maximal possible diversity product for 2/spl times/2 unitary space-time code of size 6. The construction and the optimality of the code of size 6 provide the precise value of the maximal diversity product of a 2/spl times/2 unitary space-time code of size 6.

articleTitle: Rate-distortion performance of correlated Gaussian source
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the redundancy of coding correlated Gaussian source is the same as that of the memoryless case by the random coding argument, which extends the redundancy results of Zhang, Yang and Wei on lossy source coding of memoryless sources to sources with memory in this special case.

articleTitle: Building short turbo codes with high minimum distance using 4-state tail-biting trellises
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Rate distortion with state information: bounds and interpretations
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We generate a class of lower bounds for rate distortion function with state information, based on a simplification of the rate distortion solution and a derivation of its Lagrange dual problem, which is shown to be a geometric program that extends the Lagrange dual of rate distortion R(D) without state information.

articleTitle: On asymptotic Elias bound for Euclidean space codes over distance-uniform signal sets
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The asymptotic Elias upper bound of codes designed for Hamming distance is well known. Piret and Ericsson have extended this bound for codes over symmetric PSK signal sets with Euclidean distance and for codes over signal sets that form a group, with a general distance function respectively. The tightness of these bounds depend on a choice of a probability distribution, and finding the distribution (called optimum distribution henceforth) that leads to the tightest bound is difficult in general. In B. Sundar Rajan, et al. these bounds were extended for codes over the wider class of distance-uniform signal sets. In this paper we obtain optimum distributions for codes over signal sets matched (H.A. Loeliger, 1991) to (i) dihedral group, (ii) dicyclic group, (iii) binary tetrahedral group, (iv) binary octahedral group, (v) binary icosahedral group and (vi) n-dimensional cube. Further we compare the bounds of codes over these signal sets based on the spectral rate.

articleTitle: Iterative optimization of convex divergence: applications to independent component analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Low state complexity block codes via convolutional codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Combined coding and modulation design for unknown frequency-selective channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We design complex-valued codes for transmission over frequency-selective channels that are unknown to both transmitter and receiver. The code design is optimized for joint channel estimation and data protection and outperforms standard schemes based on separate training, channel estimation and error-control.

articleTitle: New set of signals providing kidas best interpolation approximation of band-limited signals
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A tight lower bound on the classical communication cost of entanglement dilution
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we will discuss the resource of entanglement specifically, bipartite pure state entanglement. This sort of entanglement was proposed as asymptotically fungible (and thus a resource) by BBPS algorithm.

articleTitle: Precise minimax redundancy for Markov sources
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We approach the problem of finding N/sub k/ from the generating point of view. We first redefine the pair-occurence matrix on cyclic strings. We define N/sub k//sup ba/ as the number of cyclic strings starting with symbol a and ending with symbol b with the pair occurrence matrix k.

articleTitle: Distributed source coding: comparison of two methods close to the Wyner-Ziv bound
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper deals with the practical performance of distributed source coding, i.e., the compression of correlated sources that are coded independently but decoded jointly. This paper proposes to compare, in a global distortion sense, for the Gaussian continuous sources, DISCUS with another method that can be seen as an application of the Al-Issa technique.

articleTitle: Learning latent variable models with bregman divergences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Reliability and latency in binary communication
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The transmission of one of two messages over a binary symmetric channels with perfect and instantaneous feedback is considered. We study the situation where transmitter and receiver want to communicated reliably and quickly. We propose a simple decoding rule, and show that it minimizes the weighted combination of the probability of error and decoding delay for a certain range of crossover probabilities and combination weights.

articleTitle: Improved upper bound for the redundancy of fix-free codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A variable-length code is a fix-free code if no codeword is a prefix or a suffix of any other codeword. In fix-free code any finite sequence of codewords can be decoded in both directions, which can improve robustness to channel noise and speed up the decoding process. In this paper we prove a new sufficient condition for existence of fix-free codes and improve upper bound on the redundancy of optimal fix-free codes.

articleTitle: New sequence design constructions for ultra-wideband systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this work we present an explicit construction of perfect difference sets divisible by four. In addition, we also consider distinct difference sets which are a generalization of perfect difference sets. Finally, we relax our constructions in order to obtain others which are not optimal but do not have any divisibility requirements.

articleTitle: A novel scheme to reduce peak-to-average power in OFDM based on standard arrays of linear block codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A new scheme is proposed to reduce the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems by using the standard arrays of linear block codes. In our scheme, no side information needs to be transmitted and the received signal can be easily decoded by syndrome decoding.

articleTitle: Separabilities of binary Gray codes designed over Z/sub 4/
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Binary Gray codes can be designed from the Lee distance Gray codes over Z/sub 4/ with the mapping: 0/spl harr/00, 1/spl harr/01, 2/spl harr/11 and 3/spl harr/10. For these codes of length n if the Hamming distance between the Gray codes g(i) and g(j) is d, where i and j are integers, then it is proved that |i-j|>(4/15)2/sup d/ and |i-j|<2/sup n/-(4/15)2/sup d/ for d odd, and |i-j|>(7/15)2/sup d/ and |i-j|<(7/15)2/sup d/ for d even.

articleTitle: Nonlinear codes for belief propagation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We consider codes defined by a system of sparse polynomial parity check equations in F /sub 2/[x/sub 1/,...,x/sub n/]. We suggest that, defined in the right way, such codes admit an encoding comparable in efficiency with their linear counterparts (LDPC codes), and are suitable for iterative decoding.

articleTitle: Least squares kernel algorithms and applications
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Scalability and equilibrium of quality of service for high speed networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Transmission control using channel state information for cdma networks with linear mmse multi-user receivers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The uniqueness theorem for the nonextensive entropy
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Joint optimal QAM signal constellation and detector design in additive color noise channel
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes a technique for reducing the symbol error probability of a QAM communication system using a joint optimal signal constellation and a detector design method over a color noise channel. Simulation results showed the proposed design method can achieve lower symbol error than that of a conventional detector.

articleTitle: High-speed error correcting code LSI with throughput of 5 to 48 Gbps
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We proved that the hardware implementation of the proposed code and the new packet synchronization system was effectively realized by using a unique circuit configuration. A three-dimensional size-five coder and decoding-synchronization system was implemented on FPGA. The developed FPGA was applied to a high-speed MPEG communication device, which can transmit a movie signal of 20 Mbps.

articleTitle: Joint source-channel decoding of JPEG images using error resilient source codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Iterative decoding of JPEG images does not perform well due to the poor distance property of the original JPEG Huffman codes. We propose a symmetric RVLC with large free distance which can dramatically improve the system performance when iterative decoding is performed. Simulation results indicate up to 4 dB coding gain is achievable.

articleTitle: Csiszar's hypothesis testing reverse cutoff rate for general sources with memory
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Unambiguous quantum state discrimination and the equal probability measurement
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper proposes a simple suboptimal measurement for unambiguous quantum state discrimination known as the equal-probability measurement (EPM) in a quantum detection problem where a transmitter conveys classical information to a receiver using a quantum-mechanical channel.

articleTitle: On the threshold effect in the estimation of chaotic sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Self-dual codes in components of group algebras
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Properties of space-time bit-interleaved coded modulation systems in fast Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper investigate the properties of space-time bit-interleaved coded modulation (ST-BICM) systems in fast Rayleigh fading channels. We first show that ST-BICM with QPSK signaling in fast fading channels possesses the uniform distance property, which makes performance analysis tractable. We also derive the probability distribution of the squared Euclidean distance between space-time symbols assuming uniform bit-interleaving. Based on the distribution, we show that the diversity order for each codeword pair becomes maximized as the frame length becomes sufficiently long. We analyze the performance of ST-BICM in fast fading channels by deriving an FER upper bound. The derived bound turns out very accurate, requiring only the distance spectrum of the binary channel codes of ST-BICM. Numerical results demonstrate that the bound is tight enough to render an accurate estimate of performance of ST-BICM systems.

articleTitle: Optimal transform coders for classification/reconstruction with joint decoding at the receiver
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describes the optimal transform coders for classification/reconstruction with joint decoding at the receiver. The receiver acquire a probability of error and reconstructs the signal incurring a weighted mean squared error (WMSE).

articleTitle: On coherent quantum information
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper analyzes rigorously the coherent quantum information, which plays an important role in quantum information processing (quantum data processing inequality) and in quantum cryptography. We give a very brief and elegant proof for the quantum data processing inequality. We show however that the quantity is not positive in general, but positivity can be shown for pure state systems and also for classical systems. Finally, we prove that the quantity is continuous in the quantum operations.

articleTitle: Context-dependent vs. context-free: performance comparison of grammar-based codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we compare the performance of two types of universal data compression algorithms: context-dependent grammar-based (CDG-based) codes and context-free grammar-based (CFG-based) codes. The theoretical comparison of two algorithm is complicated by the following two facts observed: 1) Both CDG-based codes and CFG-based codes are universal for the class of stationary, ergodic sources with a finite alphabet; and 2) When the number of distinct contexts is upper bounded by a fixed number, the upper bounds on worst-case redundancy of CDG-based codes and CFG-based codes against any finite context arithmetic codes are in the same order of O(log log n/ log n). previously, two universal algorithms were compared only on the basis of some individual sequences. It was shown that for any sequential lossless code that is performable on a computer, there exists a sequence that is not compressible by the given code.

articleTitle: Extended binary bent sequences with optimal correlation balance properties
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The generalized binary bent sequences and bent-lifted binary sequences with optimal correlation and balance properties are introduced in [J.S. No, et al., (1997)]. In this paper, it is shown that new extended binary bent sequences can be derived from the bent-lifted binary sequences by applying the similar method used to find extended binary sequences from No sequences.

articleTitle: Information-theoretic lower bounds on the bit error probability of codes on graphs
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Adaptive blind equalization with bounded-error specification
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A novel blind equalization algorithm derived with an l/sub /spl infin// specification, featuring data-dependent selective updates, is presented.

articleTitle: The simplex codes are not optimal for binary symmetric channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: It is shown that the [2/sup K/-1,k] simplex codes are not optimal for error correction on the binary symmetric channel with bit error probability p, where 0<p<;1/2 (for k⩾3).

articleTitle: On the generation of discrete distributions from a biased coin
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: The rate of regular LDPC codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We find the rate of of a typical code from the regular LDPC ensemble. We then show that the rate of a code from the ensemble converges to the planned rate in quadratic mean and almost surely.

articleTitle: Combining low rate codes with multilevel signaling
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper we discuss the application of multilevel signaling techniques to the design of codes with spectral efficiencies between 0.75 and 1 bitldimension. We consider low rate turbo codes, along with l6QAM signal sets in a bit-interleaved coded modulation format, to achieve spectral efficiencies below 1 bitldimension. We then investigate the gains achievable with this approach compared to conventional binary signaling techniques.

articleTitle: Design of concatenated space-time block codes using signal space diversity and the Alamouti scheme
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: New full-rate space-time block codes achieving full diversity for QAM modulation using an even number of transmit antennas over quasistatic Rayleigh fading channels are proposed. The proposed codes are constructed by serially concatenating unitary rotating precoders in X. Giraud et al. (1997) and Y. Xin et al. (2001) with the Alamouti code of S. M. Alamouti (1998). The coding advantage (V. Tarokh et al., 1998) of the proposed code for a codeword pair corresponding to any distinct input pair is shown to be greater than or equal to that of the ST-CR code (Y. Xin et al., 2001).

articleTitle: On optimal linear detectors and asymptotic efficiency in multiuser detection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Capacity and cutoff rate for M-ray NCFSK signals on Rayleigh fading channels with GSC reception
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we calculate the channel capacity and cutoff rates for M-ary noncoherent FSK (NCFSK) signals on L-diversity Rayleigh fading channels when the receiver employs generalized selection combining (GSC). With GSC reception, the largest K samples among the available L square-law device outputs, for each decision hypothesis, are combined prior to the detection stage. Optimal code rates are found, based on channel capacity and cutoff rates with both hard and soft decision decoding. which minimize the required bit signal-to-noise ratio E/sub b//N/sub o/ for reliable communication. We show, through numerical results, that, for a given code rate, the GSC receiver complexity K (the order of noncoherent combining) and the modulation alphabet size M can be traded off to obtain minimum required E/sub b//N/sub o/. Also, for a given multipath diversity order L, and a given code rate, we show that diminishing returns in the minimum required E/sub b//N/sub o/ is observed by combining more multipaths.

articleTitle: How to recover the forgotten secret information
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: In this paper, we open up a brand-new field of application of error correcting codes. We present here an application of error correcting codes for the recovering of a secret information passed away accidentally due to the various reasons.

articleTitle: Finite memory universal predictability of binary sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Mismatched codebooks and the role of entropy-coding in lossy data compression
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper describe a random coding model for universal quantization. The universal quantizer consists of a (typically) mismatched random codebook followed by optimal entropy-coding. We precisely characterize the rate gain due to entropy-coding and show that it may be arbitrarily large. In the special case of entropy-coded i.i.d. Gaussian codebooks with large variance, we draw a novel connection with the compression performance of entropy-coded dithered lattice quantization. Our main tools are large deviations techniques that allow us to prove an almost sure version of the conditional limit theorem.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of large dual antenna array systems with binary modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Channel capacity and minimum probability of error for communication via large dual antenna arrays is calculated for binary modulation taking into account statistical dependencies among channel coefficients using the correlation model introduced in (R.R. Muller, 2002). Calculations rely upon the replica method developed in statistical physics (H. Nishimori, 2001).

articleTitle: Convergence analysis of SCCC and SCTCM with 'in-line' interleaver
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: This paper presents a technique for analyzing the performance of SCCC and SCTCM systems that use 'in-line' interleavers. This technique is a multidimensional extension of the well-known EXIT chart analysis, and enables us to optimize the constituent codes when in-line interleavers are used.

articleTitle: On interference cancellation and high-rate space-time codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Trace representation of binary jacobi sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: An optimal and adaptive transmit power allocation scheme for mimo system
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: An improved fast correlation attack based on list decoding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: An improvement of a recently reported powerful fast correlation attack is proposed and discussed. The proposed improvement is related to a construction of the decoding candidates list. The given theoretical analysis implies improvement of the algorithm performances assuming the same sample for processing and the same algorithm complexity.

articleTitle: Signaling over parallel channels via an input permuter
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A statistical-mechanical construction of the rate-distortion function for a binary source
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Statistical mechanics is applied to an inverse problem of linear mapping to investigate the physics of lossy compression. Rate-distortion function is derived using the RSB scheme, the state-of-the-art technique for disordered statistical systems.

articleTitle: Capacity of a multi-output channel with distributed processing
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A one dimensional (1D) and a two dimensional (2D) Kalman filters as means of distributed processing are developed for two single input multiple output (SIMO) AWGN channels, i.e., one without and the other with inter symbol interference (ISI), respectively. We show the capacity of the distributed and centrally processed channels to be the same for channels with and without ISI.

articleTitle: Differential space-time block codes with iterative detection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Various differential space-time coding schemes were proposed, where neither the transmitter nor the receiver has the channel state information (CSI). In (V. Tarokh, et al., 2000), a differential space-time block code (DSTBC) based on orthogonal designs was constructed by Tarokh and Jafarkhani (TJ). The performance of TJ'DSTBC is 3 dB worse than the corresponding coherent space-time block code (STBC). In this paper, we propose a new DSTBC scheme, which provides a coding gain due to the redundancy introduced by the differential encoder. The new code can be represented by a trellis. If the Viterbi algorithm is used in decoding, the code performs 1 dB better than TJ's scheme and is only 2 dB away from the coherent STBC (Ref. 2). Furthermore, the new scheme has a recursive structure. If concatenated with an outer code, the new scheme with iterative decoding and no CSI can outperform the corresponding concatenated STBC with ideal CSI.

articleTitle: Sum capacity of oversaturated channels based on a hierarchy of orthogonal sets
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Some oversatured channels that have been presented in the literature can be seen as hierarchies of orthogonal signature sets. We introduce a framework for oversaturated channels based on a hierarchy of orthogonal sets. The sum capacity under the equal average input energy constraint is found to depend only on the number of users in every orthogonal layer of the hierarchy. In addition to this, m-OCDMA achieves the highest sum capacity among all members of the considered hierarchy for a fixed number of users.

articleTitle: Improvement on the Ax-Katz's and Moreno-Moreno's theorems with coding theory applications
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: Improvement on the Ax-Katz's and Moreno-Moreno's theorems with coding theory applications are presented in the paper. The computation of covering radius of certain cyclic codes are also presented.

articleTitle: An improved achievable region for the discrete memoryless two-user mac with noiseless feedback
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Combined puncturing and path pruning for unequal error protection
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: A tree source and its entropy
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: A model of (i.i.d.) tree source with respect to a distribution P on nonnegative integers is given and its entropy is discussed. Furthermore, we express the probability of obtaining infinite tree, that is, of penetrating to infinity without termination for any branching distribution P.

articleTitle: A syndrome decoding of high-rate turbo codes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Sampling theorem for ISI-free communication
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: The precoder-equalizer system considered by X.G. Xia (1997) is analyzed using periodic nonuniform sampling theorem. The ISI channel is modeled as multiband channels with different spectral supports, and the channel output are periodic nonuniform sampled. We discussed the necessary and sufficient conditions of the channel and the sampling rate that allows ISI free communication. A characterization and parameterization of the precoder are derived, which can be used to construct power optimized precoders and minimum channel noise power amplification equalizers.

articleTitle: Real-time transmission of Gaussian sources over fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
abstract: We find the linear encoder and decoder pair that minimizes the mean square error in the transmission of a white Gaussian source over a Rayleigh fading channel and show that at low SNR the performance of linear coding is, to the first order, the same as the optimal performance theoretically achievable.

articleTitle: A bcjr-like labeling algorithm for tail-biting trellises
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Information-rate region and sum information rates of multi-access multi-antenna systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.

articleTitle: Signature schemes based on the DSA and the related atomic energy proxy functions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, 2003. Proceedings.
